chunks: And how many angels are in the heavens, their intercession will not avail anything except after God permits for whom He wills and approves.
ai.seo_question: When do angels' intercessions become effective according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah An-Najm is often cited to refute the notion of independent intercession (Shafa'ah) by angels or prophets, emphasizing that all authority belongs solely to Allah. It underscores the condition of 'Rida' (divine pleasure), indicating that intercession is effective only for those whom God deems worthy, thereby linking it closely to divine justice and mercy. This perspective reinforces the Shia belief in the hierarchical yet dependent nature of spiritual mediation.
